final.label: unrelated-or-unexplained-hunk
final.disposition: widen_existing (check 10). Check 10 as written keys on code hunks with removed non-comment lines and a 'What changes' identifier set. The four corpus members fire on things that procedure skips: a zero-byte file deletion (no removed line), a comment-only removal whose text names an external consumer, a qualifier added to 19 struct members in a merge PR with a one-sentence body, and compiler flags added to a CMake target. All three refuters said fix, none refuted the mechanism, and each corpus case is reproduced by one named step after the fixes: 2659 by step 4 (D stats/.gitkeep, 0 whole-word hits for 'stats' or 'gitkeep'), 3738 by step 5 (keyword grep hits once in 42 removed comment lines; `git log -m -S` names the dropping merge b815ae9ad4) and by narrowed step 6b (2 pure-removal hunks at b815ae9ad4, one cleared), 1716 by step 6a (20 added `volatile` lines absent from both first-parent source tips), 1807 by step 7 (3 added CMake lines; siblings tron and librinzler carry the same flags). The narrowed steps fire on 0 of the 38 silent tron PRs (73 A/D/R rows, 15 silent merge commits, 15 silent diffs for keywords and flags). Severity stays a question (Wade's form in all four cases).

skill_entry.name: 10. Hunk-to-claim trace (unrelated, unexplained or merge-dropped changes)
skill_entry.trigger: Always; cost one `git log`, one `git diff --name-status`, one `git show` per non-merge commit. Four sub-triggers. (a) FILE: a D or R row whose stem appears whole-word in no body sentence or commit subject (`.gitkeep` counts; an A row is at most a body gap). (b) CONSUMER COMMENT: a removed comment line naming a reader outside the compiler (DO NOT RENAME, packaging, parsed by, read by, regex, grep, CMake, script, depends on). (c) MERGE CONTENT: a merge or sync PR with added lines in no source branch, or a merge commit dropping a pure-removal hunk the branch never removed. (d) BUILD FLAG: a CMake hunk adding target_compile_options, target_compile_definitions or `-m<feature>`. Other-author commits, 'merge', 'sync' raise scan order only.
skill_entry.procedure: 1 BASE: open PR `git merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>`; merged PR `git merge-base M^1 <review commit>`. 2 Identifiers: backticked names under Changes, What changes or Summary hitting pr.diff, plus column-0 declarations of created .cpp/.hpp files; sweep PRs skip hunk scanning. 3 Hunk candidate: half its removed lines at BASE, one substantive, no identifier added; a body 'drop' sentence clears a pure removal. 4 FILE: whole-word stem grep of body and subjects. 5 CONSUMER COMMENT: candidate on its own text; name adding commit, removing commit (`git log -m -S`), consumers outside h/ src/ at BASE, origin/main. 6 MERGE: first-parent sources at review date; per merge, pure-removal hunks of `diff -U0 M^2 M`. 7 FLAG: sibling targets, intrinsic includers. 8 Revert test.
skill_entry.question: If this hunk, file row, removed comment or flag alone were reverted, would any body sentence stop being true, any PR symbol stop compiling or stop being tested, and can the author say where it came from (which commit, which source branch, which failed build)?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: A removed/added pair differing only by the rename map. Removed lines absent from BASE. A comment-only removal naming no outside reader, or one the PR's rewrite replaces (a new comment above the same code line). A pure removal a body sentence says is dropped. A file row the body or a subject names by stem. A sweep that is the PR's subject (PR 3756). Debug helpers in a hardware-attention author's own area. A build flag a sibling target already carries when the body says the target uses the feature. Formatting and include order; duplicate includes or a literal replacing a constant after a merge belong to dead-symbol and magic-literal. A merge commit as such. Never block (PR 2659).
skill_entry.finding_shape: Code hunk: "<file>:<lines> (commit <id>, '<subject>') changes <N> lines that exist at BASE and that <feature> does not touch: <what>. Reverting it alone keeps the body true. Not part of <title>; please split it out." File row, consumer comment, merge content or flag, as a question: "<file>:<BASE lines> (commit <id>, '<subject>') <deletes <path> | removes the comment '<quote>' above `<identifier>`, which survives at HEAD | adds `<qualifier or flag>` to <N> lines> that no body sentence or commit subject mentions. <Consumer at <file:line> of <rev>, or the adding commit says '<subject>' | Neither <source A> nor <source B> has these lines, so where is this coming from? | <sibling> already carries these flags; which translation unit failed?> Was this intentional?"
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: A question, never an order: "was this intentional?" (3197414598), "why did this comment get removed? It's still relevant AFAIK" (3973917755), "So where is this coming from?" (2629374536). He approves in the same review when the rest is fine: PR 2659 approved at 20:50:41Z, 26 s after the question, before the restore; PR 1807 approved one minute after the flag question with no change asked ("Hmph."). The merge-artifact wording "please clean this up... perhaps a merge artifact?" (2915281512, duplicate includes, owned by dead-symbol-no-consumer-or-definition) shows the same register. Only PR 4557 got "please split them out", for a 35-line kernel hunk inside a feature PR. Default severity: minor; normal when the removed line protects a build or packaging consumer; informational for a build flag.
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk, PR body (bot summary blocks stripped; edit history checked against the review time), commit subjects and commit parents (`git log -m -S`, `git diff -U0 M^2 M`), other files (consumers outside h/ and src/: CMakeLists.txt, cmake/, packaging/, bin/, scripts) at BASE and at origin/main, the source branches of a merge or sync PR at the review date (first-parent tips), and sibling CMake targets. Full file only for the comment block above the changed lines and for the next code line below a dropped comment. No runtime; a build-flag provenance question is asked, not answered.

## Check 10: hunk-to-claim trace (unrelated, unexplained or merge-dropped changes)

Setup for this check (overrides the common BASE line):

```
BR=$(gh pr view N --repo positron-ai/tron --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName)
# open PR:
BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD origin/$BR)
# merged PR (HEAD = the review commit, an ancestor of the base branch, so merge-base HEAD origin/$BR is HEAD itself and the diff is empty):
M=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N --jq .merge_commit_sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base $M^1 HEAD)
```
Verified: PR 2659 (base hwattention_sync) BASE=8248ebbe72, `git diff --name-status BASE eb0627f006` = 2 rows (against origin/main: 178 rows); PR 1716 BASE=37cfc477fb, 2 files +48/-19 (first parent of the oldest PR commit, 7f993bc2db, gives 50 files because it includes main's merged changes); PR 1807 BASE=e61f0b0ab7 (= d03129dad0~2).
Body: strip `<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->` ... `<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->` from body.md. Body date: `gh api graphql -f query='{repository(owner:"positron-ai",name:"tron"){pullRequest(number:N){userContentEdits(first:20){nodes{editedAt editor{login}}}}}}'`; an edit later than the review means a clearance sentence may not have been visible to the reviewer (PR 3738: 17 edits, last 2026-09-09T23:15:23Z, review 23:25Z).
Author map: `gh api users/<login> --jq .name` before binning (PR 3738: login BillBaumann = 'Bill Baumann', 7 commits; 29 commits by 'Chander Luderman Miller', login chander-positron).

1. Identifier set: backticked names and Note titles under the first heading whose text contains "What changes", "Changes" or "Summary" (the whole stripped body when none exists), minus names with 0 hits in pr.diff (PR 3738: `t_mwaitx`, a flaky test cited in the test plan) and minus command-line flags (`--tracer-core`) that no C++ line carries verbatim. A body name that exists at BASE stays in the set (PR 3756: `process_device_id`). From each created .cpp/.hpp file add `git show HEAD:FILE | grep -E '^(struct|class|static|constexpr|inline|using|TEST_CASE)'` (t/t_fpga_tracer.cpp: 34 TEST_CASEs, 56 column-0 lines); a created .md file adds none. When the body has no backticked code name, or every one is a test target or commit id (PR 4353: `t_llama_unit`, `t_ranged_mask`, `282955f1`), take the function, member and parameter names the diff declares in `+` lines. Write the list with its `grep -c` count over pr.diff.
2. Bin commits from log.txt (SIDE / MAIN-FEATURE as in SKILL.md). Sweep PR: the title or body says "throughout", "everywhere", "all call sites", "rename" or "use X ... throughout" and one identifier appears in at least half of the diff files (PR 3756: process_device_id in 29 of 36 files); then skip step 3 and run only steps 4-7. Steps 4-7 run over the BASE..HEAD diff, not per commit: a line a merge commit dropped is in no non-merge commit (PR 3738: 26 non-merge commits, 624 hunks, none carries the DO NOT RENAME removal). Scan every non-merge commit, SIDE first: `git show <sha> -- FILE` per file.
3. Candidate hunk test: at least half of its `-` lines in `git show BASE:FILE` verbatim, at least one not blank, brace-only or comment-only, no identifier in the `+` lines. Inheritance within the same function or TEST_CASE. A hunk with no `+` lines is a candidate only when none of its removed lines names an identifier that a body sentence says is dropped, removed or replaced (PR 2875 "Drop `mark_used`/`mark_unused`/`check_usage`" clears full.hpp:419, :512 and token_cache.cpp:162).
4. FILE rows: `git -C WT diff --name-status BASE..HEAD | grep -E '^(A|D|R)'`. For each path P: STEM=$(basename P | sed 's/\..*//'); grep body.md and log.txt with `grep -i -w -c -F "$STEM"`, again with `_` and `-` in STEM replaced by a space, and `grep -i -c -F "$(dirname P)/"` for the directory with its trailing slash. A one-letter directory (t/, h/) never clears; a substring hit never clears ('doc' inside 'documented'). Zero hits on every form: a D or R row is a candidate; an A row is a body gap at most, and never a candidate when another hunk of pr.diff uses a name the file declares (PR 2774 h/common/fixed_string.hpp: `fixed_string`, `expert_labels` used in feed_forward.hpp). Name the commit: `git -C WT log --diff-filter=AD --format='%h %s' BASE..HEAD -- P`. Verified: 73 A/D/R rows in the 38 silent tron PRs give 0 candidates (basename-only grep gave 3: PR 1722 hwattention.hpp/.cpp, body "Added hwattention files."; PR 2774 fixed_string.hpp); PR 3738: `t_fpga_tracer` 1 whole-word body hit clears t/t_fpga_tracer.cpp, "fpga tracing" 3 subject hits clear doc/fpga-tracing.md.
5. CONSUMER COMMENT lines: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE..HEAD | grep -n -E '^-\s*(//|\*|#)' | grep -i -E 'DO NOT RENAME|DO NOT REMOVE|packag|parsed by|read by|regex|grep|cmake|script|depend'`. Every hit is a candidate on the strength of its own text; the greps below corroborate and are reported either way. (a) Adding commit: `git -C WT log --format='%h %ci %s' -S'<comment text>' origin/main -- FILE | tail -1`. (b) Consumer: take the identifiers on the lines below the comment at BASE, cut each to its stem before the last underscore (`min_bitfile`; CMake builds the full name from a variable, so the full identifier never matches), and run `git -C WT grep -n '<stem>' <rev> -- ':!h' ':!src'` at BASE and at origin/main. (c) Removing commit: `git -C WT log -m --format='%h %p %s' -S'<comment text>' HEAD -- FILE` (`-m` is required; a merge commit's conflict resolution does not show without it). Digest check: the regex hits 3 of 67 digests; 3738 is the true positive; 3093 ("default OFF" rewritten to "default ON") and 4191 ("I depend on `tok`" rewritten) are cleared by step 8 because the PR's own rewrite replaces the line.
6. MERGE CONTENT. (a) Added lines: runs only when the PR title or body says it merges or syncs a named branch (PR 1716 "Second step of AoF merge") or the base_ref is a sync branch. Sources = the branches at the review date: `git rev-list -1 --first-parent --before=<comment timestamp> origin/<branch>` (`--first-parent` is required: without it the origin/main lookup for PR 1716 returns the PR's own commit 2d7f3a62ec, which carries the 19 `volatile` members, and the check would not fire). For every added line of `git diff -U0 BASE..HEAD` run `git -C WT grep -q -F -- '<line>' <src> -- FILE` in each source; lines absent from every source are candidates, grouped by file. A feature PR whose history only contains merge-of-main commits does not run 6a: every added line of such a PR is absent from main by construction (PR 3738: all 62 hunks would fire). (b) Dropped lines: for each merge commit M in `git log --merges --format=%h BASE..HEAD`, run `git -C WT diff -U0 M^2 M` and keep only hunks with `-` lines and no `+` line (a rewritten statement is not a drop). Keep a hunk only when at least one removed non-blank line is present at M^1 or absent at `git merge-base M^1 M^2` (the branch side did not remove it on purpose) and `git -C WT grep -F '<line>' M -- h src t CMakeLists.txt cmake` finds the line nowhere at M (a line found elsewhere was moved). Clear a surviving hunk when HEAD carries a new comment above the same code line, or when the dropped line names a symbol absent at HEAD (it could not compile). Each remaining hunk is a candidate; name M and quote the lines. Do not run `git diff M^2 M` over whole files: it lists the PR's own edits (PR 3738: 128-177 removed lines per merge, 10 merges, 32,990 diff lines). Verified: b815ae9ad4 (PR 3738) keeps 2 pure-removal hunks in h/pos/config.hpp, `@@ -104,3` (DO NOT RENAME block, candidate) and `@@ -69,2` (`static_assert(fpga_use_period % tracer_period == 0`, cleared: `tracer_period` has 0 hits in config.hpp at 819d4c96b8); the 15 merge commits of silent PRs 4353, 1739, 1707 and 1722 keep 0.
7. BUILD FLAG: `git -C WT diff BASE..HEAD -- '*CMakeLists.txt' '*.cmake' | grep -n -E '^\+.*(target_compile_options|target_compile_definitions|add_compile_definitions|(^|[:;" ])-m[a-z0-9]+)'` (the file restriction and the token boundary are required: over whole diffs `-m[a-z0-9]+` hits 6 prose lines of PR 2475 t/t_clearhbm.cpp, 'direct-mode'). Sibling targets: `git -C WT grep -n -E 'mavx512|mavx2|mfma|TRON_AVX512_ENABLED' HEAD -- '*CMakeLists.txt'`. Translation units that need the flag: `git -C WT grep -l -E 'immintrin|_mm512|_mm256|simd.hpp' HEAD -- h/<lib> src/<lib>`. Report the question, not a split.
8. Clearance: rename-map identity; a GitHub review thread id; a body sentence or commit subject describing the added content, the file row or the removal ("Restore the bitfile packaging warning" clears its own hunk). A sentence naming only the file or callee does not clear; a contradicting sentence is quoted. For a consumer comment, clear only when a consumer existed at the adding commit and no longer exists at HEAD; a consumer absent at BASE but named by the adding commit's subject does not clear (PR 3738: the CMake reader entered main five days after the review); a commit message that names the identifiers below the comment but not the comment (b815ae9ad4 "Restore the upstream bitfile version constants so the merged tree builds") does not clear.
9. Test hunks: callee untouched by the PR -> unrelated; callee rewritten -> regression guard, body gap at most.
10. Revert test (all kinds): reverting the item alone keeps every body sentence true, every identifier compiling, and every assertion passing at HEAD also passing at BASE. If the hunk is the sole test of a PR symbol's forwarded behavior, report a body gap and let the author choose.
11. One finding per hunk, file row, removed comment block or flag line.

On PR 4557: ec795fbce8 (src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp:152-181, 35 of 36 removed lines at BASE, 0 identifiers, body:52 "The tile loads are unchanged" contradicts) -> unrelated, split out. 39a6899446 carries t/t_heap_v2.cpp:1209-1223 (CHECK is_aligned, contract alloc_align at BASE memory.hpp:146); it is the only test of the new operator new[]'s alignment forwarding -> body gap, author's choice. 959d1ae229 partner-zero rows: callee append_v_row rewritten by the PR -> regression guard, not unrelated.
